notes.title: Organization Activities
notes.summary: Saudi Ceramic Company is a Saudi joint stock company established by Royal Decree No. (M/16) on 14 April 1977 (Commercial Register 1010014590, Riyadh), engaged in the production and sale of ceramic products, water heaters and related components, and the import of related machinery and equipment. The consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024 cover the parent and three subsidiaries: Ceramic Pipes Company (77.89%; 2023: 73.89%), Arzan Company (100%) and Ceramics Investment Company (98.69% per the table; the footnote states 98.89%, being 95% direct and 3.89% indirect through Ceramic Pipes Company). On 4 July 2024 the Company acquired an additional 4% of Ceramic Pipes Company under a waiver agreement with shareholder Khaled Saleh Abdulaziz Al Rajhi. Arzan Company and Ceramics Investment Company had not started commercial operations by 31 December 2024.

notes.title: Basis of Preparation
notes.summary: The consolidated financial statements are prepared under IFRS as endorsed in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and other SOCPA pronouncements, on the historical cost convention except where IFRS requires another measurement basis (Note 4). They are presented in Saudi Riyals rounded to the nearest thousand and consolidate the parent and all subsidiaries listed in Note 1, all with a 31 December year-end, with intra-group balances eliminated. Amendments effective 1 January 2024 (IAS 1 classification of liabilities, IFRS 16 sale and leaseback, IAS 7/IFRS 7 supplier finance arrangements) had no material effect; IAS 21 (2025), IFRS 9/IFRS 7 (2026), IFRS 18 and IFRS 19 (2027) are not yet applied and are expected to have no material impact.

subnotes.summary: IFRS as endorsed in KSA and other SOCPA standards and pronouncements.

subnotes.title: Basis of measurement
subnotes.summary: Historical cost except where IFRS requires otherwise; judgements and estimates per Note 4.

subnotes.summary: Saudi Riyal; all amounts rounded to the nearest thousand unless otherwise indicated.

subnotes.title: Basis of consolidation

subnotes.title: New standards and amendments to standards and interpretations

notes.title: Material Accounting Estimates and Assumptions
notes.summary: The note lists the areas of significant judgement: employees' post-employment benefits (actuarial valuation using the projected unit credit method), impairment of inventories (net realisable value, with replacement cost used for raw materials and spare parts), impairment of non-financial assets (recoverable amount as the higher of value in use and fair value less costs to sell at CGU level), fair value measurement (three-level hierarchy; no transfers between levels in 2024 or 2023) and useful lives of property, plant and equipment. A change in accounting estimate effective 1 January 2024 depreciates leasehold improvements over the lower of useful life or the expected (rather than contractual) lease term, applied prospectively, decreasing depreciation expense and increasing net profit by SAR 2.3 million. Management concluded there are no material doubts about the Group's ability to continue as a going concern.
notes.investorRelevance: Contains the explicit going-concern conclusion and a prospective change in depreciation estimate that lifted 2024 net profit by SAR 2.3 million.

flag.text: Change in accounting estimate from 1 January 2024: leasehold improvements now depreciated over the lower of useful life or expected lease term, reducing depreciation and increasing net profit by SAR 2.3 million; management reports no material doubt about going concern.

notes.title: Material Accounting Policies
notes.summary: Sets out the accounting policies applied consistently to all periods presented. It covers cash and cash equivalents, property, plant and equipment (straight-line depreciation; buildings 10-33.33 years, furniture 4-10, vehicles 4, tools 10; leasehold improvements over the lower of useful life or expected lease term, extended to 10 years for some locations in 2024), capital work in progress, assets held for sale, IFRS 16 leases, intangible assets (15 years), the equity method for associates, inventories at the lower of weighted-average cost and net realisable value, borrowings and borrowing costs, payables, unfunded end-of-service benefits under IAS 19, foreign currency, zakat, provisions and contingent liabilities, earnings per share, segment reporting, treasury shares, IFRS 15 revenue recognition (including trade discounts, sale-or-return showroom sales with a refund liability and target-based wholesale incentives netted against receivables), expense classification, IFRS 9 classification of financial assets (amortised cost or FVOCI) and liabilities, and impairment of financial (simplified ECL) and non-financial assets.

subnotes.title: Cash and cash equivalents
subnotes.summary: Cash, bank balances and highly liquid investments maturing within three months, available without restriction; cash flow statement prepared under the indirect method.

subnotes.title: Property, plant and equipment
subnotes.summary: Cost less depreciation and impairment, straight-line over useful lives (buildings 10-33.33 years, furniture 4-10, vehicles 4, tools 10, leasehold improvements over the lower of useful life or expected lease term); 2024 internal review extended the maximum leasehold improvement life to 10 years for some locations instead of 4.

subnotes.title: Capital work in progress (CWIP)
subnotes.summary: Stated at cost less impairment and transferred to the relevant PP&E category when ready for use.

subnotes.title: Assets held for sale
subnotes.summary: Measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell when sale is highly probable within twelve months; not depreciated and presented as current.

subnotes.title: Right-of-use assets and lease liabilities
subnotes.summary: Leases of warehouses, offices and showrooms recognised on balance sheet; ROU assets depreciated over the shorter of useful life and lease term; short-term and low-value leases expensed; extension options included only when reasonably certain.

subnotes.title: Trade receivables
subnotes.summary: Stated net of the provision for expected credit losses and the provision for customers' incentive.

subnotes.title: Intangible assets
subnotes.summary: Cost less amortisation and impairment, amortised straight-line over 15 years.

subnotes.title: Investments in associate
subnotes.summary: Entities over which the Group has significant influence are accounted for using the equity method.

subnotes.title: Inventories
subnotes.summary: Lower of cost (weighted average, including production overheads at normal capacity) and net realisable value.

subnotes.title: Borrowings
subnotes.summary: Initially at fair value net of transaction costs, then amortised cost using the effective interest method; classified as current unless settlement can be deferred at least 12 months.

subnotes.title: Borrowing costs
subnotes.summary: Capitalised on qualifying assets taking more than one year to get ready for use, excluding idle periods; all other borrowing costs expensed.

subnotes.title: Trade and other payables
subnotes.summary: Trade payables recognised at invoice amount and measured at amortised cost; accruals at the best estimate of amounts payable.

subnotes.title: Employees' post-employment benefits
subnotes.summary: Unfunded end-of-service defined benefit plan under Saudi Labor Law, valued annually by the projected unit credit method with remeasurements in OCI; short-term benefits accrued undiscounted.

subnotes.title: Foreign currency transactions
subnotes.summary: Recorded at spot rate; monetary items retranslated at the reporting-date rate with differences taken to profit or loss.

subnotes.title: Zakat provision
subnotes.summary: Calculated under ZATCA rules and charged as a separate line in profit or loss; differences on prior-year assessments recognised in the year of final settlement.

subnotes.title: Provisions
subnotes.summary: Recognised for probable, reliably measurable obligations from past events, discounted at a pre-zakat rate with unwinding charged as interest expense.

subnotes.title: Contingent Liability
subnotes.summary: Possible obligations, or present obligations with improbable or unmeasurable outflows, are disclosed but not recognised.

subnotes.title: Earnings per share
subnotes.summary: Net profit for the year divided by the weighted average number of shares outstanding.

subnotes.title: Segmental reporting
subnotes.summary: Operating segments reviewed by the Chief Operating Decision Maker, aggregated where economic characteristics are similar.

subnotes.title: Treasury Shares
subnotes.summary: Own shares acquired for the Employee Share Program are held at cost as a deduction from equity; no gain or loss is recognised in profit or loss.

subnotes.title: Revenue recognition
subnotes.summary: IFRS 15 five-step model with revenue at a point in time on delivery; retail discounts deducted upfront, wholesale discounts accrued monthly and settled by credit note, showroom sale-or-return with a refund liability, and target-based wholesale incentives provided monthly and netted against receivables.

subnotes.title: Expenses
subnotes.summary: Accrual basis; production costs classified as cost of sales, selling costs as selling and marketing expenses, remainder as general and administrative.

subnotes.title: Financial instruments
subnotes.summary: Financial assets measured at amortised cost (SPPI) or FVOCI (irrevocable election for equity investments, gains held in other reserve and never recycled); financial liabilities (bank borrowings, trade and other payables) at amortised cost; offsetting only with a legal right and intention to net settle.

subnotes.title: Impairment of financial assets
subnotes.summary: Forward-looking expected credit losses; simplified lifetime ECL for trade receivables grouped by credit characteristics and days past due, adjusted for macroeconomic factors such as inflation and GDP growth.

subnotes.title: Impairment of Non-Financial Assets
subnotes.summary: Recoverable amount is the higher of fair value less costs to sell and value in use at CGU level; impairment recognised immediately in profit or loss and reversed only up to the carrying amount net of depreciation that would otherwise have existed.

notes.title: Property, Plant and Equipment, Net
notes.summary: Property, plant and equipment had a net book value of SAR 1,546,358 thousand at 31 December 2024 (2023: 1,513,398) after additions of 203,034 (of which 166,531 to assets under construction, mainly the new porcelain tile factory and production-line efficiency projects), depreciation of 117,142 (2023: 122,954) and impairment losses of 51,070 (2023: 78,224 plus 136,880 of fire damage). The 2024 impairment comprises SAR 45 million on the Red Bricks business unit, whose recoverable amount of SAR 76 million (fair value less cost of disposal) was below its SAR 121 million carrying amount after five-year budgets showed negative operating income, and SAR 5.7 million on Ceramic Pipes Company (2023: SAR 78.2 million), whose value in use of SAR 88.1 million uses a 12% pre-tax discount rate, a negative gross margin of 42% and management's intention to liquidate the business post 2027. Buildings, machinery and equipment with a carrying amount of SAR 379 million (2023: SAR 908 million) are pledged as security for SIDF loans (Note 16), and borrowing costs of SAR 9.1 million (2023: SAR 8.5 million) were capitalised to assets under construction.

Ceramic tiles and sanitary ware contributed 887,470 (2023: 851,290), water heaters 429,828 (2023: 431,215), red brick 12,278 and ceramic pipes 19,221. Local sales grew to 1,243,403 (2023: 1,187,322) while exports fell to 105,394 (2023: 127,546), of which water heaters account for 82,743. Contract balances comprise receivables of 308,668, a provision for customers' incentives of 65,207 (Note 10) and a refund liability of 32,745 (Note 18).

notes.title: Operating Segments
notes.summary: The Group reports three segments reviewed monthly by the CEO: ceramic tiles and sanitary ware, water heaters and ceramic pipes; red bricks, plastic, packaging, head office and desert mines are below the reportable thresholds. Segment revenue was 1,348,797 in 2024 (2023: 1,314,868) and the segment loss before zakat narrowed to (71,194) (2023: (216,049)), with water heaters the only profitable segment at 45,849 against losses of (83,872) in tiles and sanitary ware and (33,171) in Ceramic Pipes Company; impairment losses of (51,070) were charged to tiles (45,357) and ceramic pipes (5,713). Segment assets were 2,676,609 and liabilities 1,251,909. Revenue by geography was Saudi Arabia 1,243,403, other GCC countries 81,742 and other countries 23,652, all property, plant and equipment is located in Saudi Arabia, and the five largest customers accounted for approximately 39% of revenue (2023: 37%).

notes.title: Financial Instruments, Risk Management and Fair Value
notes.summary: Financial assets of 312,624 (2023: 357,219) comprise the FVOCI investment of 7,877 (Level 3) and 304,747 at amortised cost; financial liabilities of 946,375 (2023: 1,033,886) are all at amortised cost (short-term loans 405,855, long-term loans 329,990, trade payables 210,530). Credit risk centres on gross trade receivables of 308,668, 86.2% in Saudi Arabia and 13.6% in other GCC countries, with the five largest customers representing approximately 47% of receivables (2023: 40%); 33,055 of receivables are more than 270 days past due with a 62.45% expected loss rate, driving most of the 21,483 ECL allowance, and SAR 241,000 was written off. Contractual undiscounted financial liabilities total 1,053,078, of which 834,038 fall due within one year, against cash of SAR 42.3 million held with banks rated BBB+ or above. Variable-rate borrowings of SAR 559 million (2023: SAR 627 million) expose income to (5,590) per 100 basis point rise; foreign exchange risk is considered insignificant given the SAR/USD peg, and capital is monitored through a net debt to equity gearing ratio.

notes.title: Significant Events
notes.summary: On 15 July 2023 a fire in the sanitary ware department of the Group's second factory damaged machinery and equipment with a book value of SAR 136.8 million (Note 5) and inventories costing SAR 27.9 million (Note 9), both charged to costs. The factory is insured for such losses and for business interruption; the Group has submitted its claim and all required documents, but the insurer's evaluation of the claim was still in progress at the date of these financial statements. Management believes the insurance coverage is sufficient to cover the losses.
notes.investorRelevance: The July 2023 factory fire destroyed PP&E of SAR 136.8 million and inventory of SAR 27.9 million, and the insurance claim, including business interruption, was still unresolved when the 2024 statements were issued.

notes.title: Restatement and Reclassification of Comparative Information
notes.summary: The Company restated and reclassified prior-period balances at 31 December 2023 and 1 January 2023. Trade and other receivables were reduced by 62,802 (to 286,865) and 35,843 (to 275,341) as the provision for customers' incentive, foreign exchange gains and losses and customer advances were moved out of trade and other payables; cash and cash equivalents fell by 923 (to 63,754) and 1,103 (to 69,590); accrued finance costs were reclassified from payables into short-term borrowings (1,257 and 674) and the current portion of long-term borrowings (9,342 and 8,436); and trade and other payables fell by (74,325) (to 341,096) and (46,056) (to 369,989). The 2023 cash flow statement was also restated (provision for customers' incentive 32,153, trade and other receivables (5,194), finance cost paid 2,737, trade and other payables (29,515)). The changes have no impact on profit or loss, other comprehensive income, equity or basic and diluted loss per share for 2023 or 2022.
